subject: Re: FinWave discovery \u2014 model fit, evals & quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finwave.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: FinWave discovery — model fit, evals & quantization tradeoffs

Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + entity extraction for follow-up routing.
- Target latency: 150-300ms p95 for single-request generation (US region).
- Throughput target: ~15k tokens/min sustained for peak processing.
- Quality requirement: human-grade summarization with <=5% error on NER.

Model fit recommendations (initial list to evaluate)
- Llama-2-70B-instruct (fp16 baseline) — strong quality; heavier on compute.
- Mistral-Instruct-70B — competitive quality/cost balance.
- RW-optimized-13B (Redwood-verified) — candidate for aggressive quantization.

Quantization / throughput notes (what we suggest testing)
- AWQ (4/8-bit hybrid): best throughput uplift with minimal quality delta in many of our tests; good first pass for non-crit tasks.
- GPTQ (4-bit): higher risk of small regression on entity extraction; worth validating on your prompt set.
- FP8 / bf8 inference (if supported): promising throughput with small arithmetic differences; run in parallel when possible.

Attachments: I attached a short trade-study spreadsheet (quantization-tradeoffs-20270410.xlsx) and our eval prompt set (finwave-eval-prompt-set-v3.txt).

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm the evaluation prompt set (attached). If edits needed, mark the prompts you want prioritized.
2) We (Redwood) run a 72-hour trade study across the three models above with AWQ + GPTQ + fp16 baselines and deliver: quality delta (F1/N-ER), p95 latency, and cost/unit.
3) Align on pass/fail thresholds for regression (we recommend <2% NER degradation for production).
4) Follow-up call to review results and agree on production quantization profile + rollout plan.

Owner / points of contact
- Marissa Cole (Sales, Redwood) — commercial lead.
- Dev Patel (Applied ML / Eval lead, Redwood) — technical lead, will run and interpret trade studies.

Doable to start next week? If yes, what time zones look best for your engineering lead to join a short kickoff (30 min)?

Thanks — look forward to running the benchmarks.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: FinWave discovery — model fit, evals & quantization tradeoffs

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirmed: our primary use case is the support summarization + routing. Couple quick clarifications: 

- Throughput: 15k tokens/min is correct. For latency, 200ms p95 would be ideal; 300ms is our upper bound.
- Quality/regression: we can accept up to ~1.5% NER drop, but summarization ROUGE loss should be under ~3% relative to your fp16 baseline.

I've attached our internal latency/SLO doc for context (finwave-capacity-requirements.pdf).

We approve the proposed trade study plan — please proceed. Our engineering lead (Samir Patel) will join the kickoff; cc'ing him shortly in calendar.

Also: two quick asks before you kick off tests:
1) Can you include a raw-output diff sample for a handful of prompts so our QA can quickly eyeball qualitative regressions?
2) Can you flag any prompts in the set that you consider high-sensitivity for NER?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, FinWave
alex@finwave.com
[attachment: finwave-capacity-requirements.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finwave.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinWave discovery — model fit, evals & quantization tradeoffs

Alex — perfect, thanks for the thresholds and the SLO doc. We'll include the raw-output diffs in the deliverable (sample size: 50 prompts across high/med/low sensitivity).

On prompt sensitivity: we've flagged ~12 prompts in the attached prompt set as high-sensitivity for NER (comments inline in finwave-eval-prompt-set-v3.txt). If you have additions, please highlight them.

Technical plan (high level)
- Baselines: fp16 inference on Llama-2-70B & Mistral-70B to establish quality baseline.
- Quantization runs: AWQ 4/8 hybrid and GPTQ-4 for each candidate model; RW-optimized-13B will also be evaluated as a lower-cost option with aggressive quantization.
- Metrics: NER F1, summary ROUGE-L, p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
- Deliverable: spreadsheet + raw-output samples + Jupyter notebook with plots + recommended production profile.

Dylan / Dev — acting items: please provision the runs (AWQ + GPTQ + fp16 baselines) on the dedicated test pool and kick off once Alex confirms Samir's availability. Target: complete trade study in 72 hours from start.

Alex — I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute kickoff; proposed times Wed/Thu morning PST.

—
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: FinWave discovery — model fit, evals & quantization tradeoffs

Team — quick internal action list before we hit the external kickoff:
1) Dev: spin up test pool (4x A100 equivalent) with latest runtime + AWQ & GPTQ toolchains. Use the RW-optimized-13B checkpoint + Llama-2-70B + Mistral-70B.
2) Use the attached prompt set (v3). Tag prompts marked as HIGH for separate reporting.
3) Collect: p95 latency (cold & warm), tokens/sec, NER F1, ROUGE-L, and disk/memory footprint. Export raw-output diffs for 50 samples (as Marissa outlined).
4) Estimated runtime: 48-72 hours depending on queue. Notify when first 12-hour batch finishes.

I'll coordinate pricing delta calc once we have tokens/sec and p95.

—Dylan
